title: Care Academy Q&A: Goodwill Frequency and the Late-Delivery Make-Good
content:
**Rule.** On a Delivery Claims Late Delivery Claim, the goodwill frequency multiplier depends on the Goodwill Credits issued to the customer in the trailing 12 calendar months: two or more multiply the make-good by 0.50, exactly one by 0.75, and none leaves it as it is.

| Goodwill Credits issued to the customer in the trailing 12 calendar months | Multiplier on the make-good |
|---|---|
| none | 1 — as it is |
| exactly 1 | 0.75 |
| 2 or more | 0.50 |

**Which records show these Goodwill Credits?**
The customer's Gift Cards & Store Credit instruments of the type Goodwill Credit. Each instrument shows its issue date.

**Which ones are counted?**
Every Goodwill Credit instrument issued to the customer with an issue date in the 12 calendar months up to today, whatever it was issued for and whatever its balance now.

**Does a Goodwill Credit issued 13 months ago count?**
No. Only issue dates inside the trailing 12 calendar months count.

**Do other kinds of stored value count — Return Store Credit, a Marlowe Rewards Note, a gift card?**
No. Only instruments of the type Goodwill Credit are counted.

**Hypothetical case.** A customer holds two Goodwill Credits issued 2 months and 14 months ago and a Return Store Credit issued last week. One Goodwill Credit falls in the window, so the make-good is multiplied by 0.75: a make-good of 16.00 USD becomes 12.00 USD on this multiplier.
